summary: The Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts issued a statement on Dec 11 condemning the Thai military for shelling the 11th-century Ta Krabey Temple in Oddar Meanchey province. The ministry claims the temple, already damaged on Dec 9, suffered complete devastation due to renewed shelling on Dec 10 and 11.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence released a casualty report on Dec 11, stating that as of Dec 10, Thai incursions had killed 10 Cambodian civilians, including an infant, and injured 60 others. The ministry called on the international community to condemn these 'war crimes'.

summaryTh: กระทรวงกลาโหมกัมพูชาเปิดเผยรายงานผู้เสียชีวิตและบาดเจ็บเมื่อวันที่ 11 ธันวาคม โดยระบุว่า ณ วันที่ 10 ธันวาคม การรุกรานของไทยทำให้พลเรือนกัมพูชาเสียชีวิต 10 ราย รวมถึงทารกหนึ่งคน และบาดเจ็บ 60 ราย ทางกระทรวงเรียกร้องให้ประชาคมโลกประณาม 'อาชญากรรมสงคราม' เหล่านี้

summary: The Permanent Mission of Cambodia to the UN issued an urgent appeal on Dec 11, 2025, requesting the Security Council to demand that Thai forces cease their 'illegal armed aggression'. This follows heavy shelling and F-16 airstrikes reported by Phnom Penh.

summary: Detailed military report of front-line clashes across multiple zones. On the morning of Dec 11, Cambodian forces responded with BM21 rockets at the Battle of Boeung Trakuan. In the 4th Military Zone, Thai forces allegedly used tanks and artillery starting from 4:40 AM near Khnar Temple and Preah Vihear. In the 5th Military Zone, Thai drones reportedly dropped bombs in Pursat and Banteay Meanchey provinces.

In the 4th Military Zone, Thai forces allegedly used tanks and artillery starting from 4:40 AM near Khnar Temple and Preah Vihear. In the 5th Military Zone, Thai drones reportedly dropped bombs in Pursat and Banteay Meanchey provinces.

summary: The article details the escalating conflict, accusing Thailand of launching a full-scale assault, including air, artillery, and naval strikes across multiple Cambodian border provinces. It reports that a baby was among the nine people killed as the fighting entered its fourth day, emphasizing the deadly impact on civilian populations.

summaryKh: អត្ថបទនេះរៀបរាប់លម្អិតអំពីជម្លោះដែលកំពុងតែកើនឡើង ដោយចោទប្រកាន់ប្រទេសថៃថា បានបើកការវាយប្រហារទ្រង់ទ្រាយធំ រួមទាំងការវាយប្រហារតាមអាកាស កាំភ្លើងធំ និងកងទ័ពជើងទឹកឆ្លងកាត់ខេត្តព្រំដែនកម្ពុជាជាច្រើន។ វារាយការណ៍ថា ទារកម្នាក់ស្ថិតក្នុងចំណោមមនុស្ស 9 នាក់ដែលបានស្លាប់ ខណៈការប្រយុទ្ធបានឈានចូលដល់ថ្ងៃទី4 ដោយសង្កត់ធ្ងន់លើផលប៉ះពាល់ធ្ងន់ធ្ងរដល់ជនស៊ីវិល។
summaryTh: บทความนี้ให้รายละเอียดถึงความขัดแย้งที่ทวีความรุนแรงขึ้น โดยกล่าวหาว่าไทยได้เปิดฉากการโจมตีเต็มรูปแบบ ซึ่งรวมถึงการโจมตีทางอากาศ ปืนใหญ่ และเรือในหลายจังหวัดชายแดนของกัมพูชา รายงานว่ามีทารกคนหนึ่งอยู่ในกลุ่มผู้เสียชีวิต 9 ราย ขณะที่การสู้รบเข้าสู่วันที่สี่ โดยเน้นย้ำถึงผลกระทบที่ร้ายแรงต่อพลเรือน

summary: Cambodia's UN representative Keo Chhea sent a letter to the UN Security Council on Dec 10, reporting that Thai incursions had killed 10 Cambodian civilians, including an infant, and injured 60 others. The letter requested urgent intervention and cited violations of the UN Charter and the July 2025 ceasefire.
summaryEn: Cambodia's UN representative Keo Chhea sent a letter to the UN Security Council on Dec 10, reporting that Thai incursions had killed 10 Cambodian civilians, including an infant, and injured 60 others. The letter requested urgent intervention and cited violations of the UN Charter and the July 2025 ceasefire.
summaryKh: តំណាងកម្ពុជាប្រចាំអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ លោក កែវ ឈា បានផ្ញើលិខិតទៅកាន់ក្រុមប្រឹក្សាសន្តិសុខអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិនៅថ្ងៃទី 10 ខែធ្នូ ដោយរាយការណ៍ថា ការឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃបានសម្លាប់ជនស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា 10 នាក់ រួមទាំងទារកម្នាក់ និងរបួស 60 នាក់ផ្សេងទៀត។ លិខិតនោះបានស្នើសុំការជ្រៀតជ្រែកជាបន្ទាន់ និងបានលើកឡើងពីការរំលោភលើធម្មនុញ្ញអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ និងបទឈប់បាញ់ខែកក្កដា ឆ្នាំ 2025។
summaryTh: นายแก้ว เชีย ผู้แทนกัมพูชาประจำ UN ได้ส่งหนังสือถึงคณะมนตรีความมั่นคงแห่งสหประชาชาติเมื่อวันที่ 10 ธ.ค. โดยรายงานว่าการรุกรานของไทยทำให้พลเรือนกัมพูชาเสียชีวิต 10 ราย รวมถึงทารก 1 ราย และบาดเจ็บ 60 ราย จดหมายดังกล่าวเรียกร้องให้มีการแทรกแซงอย่างเร่งด่วน โดยอ้างถึงการละเมิดกฎบัตร UN และข้อตกลงหยุดยิงเดือนกรกฎาคม 2568

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense (MND) firmly denied reports by Thai media outlets, such as Thai Tribune, which accused Cambodia of employing foreign mercenaries to fly suicide drones in the border conflict. The MND condemned the reports as "false, fabricated, and smear campaigns" intended to divert attention from Thailand's own violations of international law and justify the use of more brutal weapons against Cambodia.
summaryEn: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense (MND) firmly denied reports by Thai media outlets, such as Thai Tribune, which accused Cambodia of employing foreign mercenaries to fly suicide drones in the border conflict. The MND condemned the reports as "false, fabricated, and smear campaigns" intended to divert attention from Thailand's own violations of international law and justify the use of more brutal weapons against Cambodia.

summaryTh: กระทรวงกลาโหมของกัมพูชาปฏิเสธอย่างหนักแน่นต่อรายงานของสื่อไทย เช่น Thai Tribune ที่กล่าวหากัมพูชาว่าใช้ทหารรับจ้างต่างชาติในการบินโดรนฆ่าตัวตายในความขัดแย้งชายแดน กระทรวงกลาโหมประณามรายงานดังกล่าวว่าเป็น “ข้อมูลเท็จ สร้างเรื่อง และเป็นการใส่ร้าย” ที่มีจุดประสงค์เพื่อเบี่ยงเบนความสนใจจากการละเมิดกฎหมายระหว่างประเทศของไทย และเพื่อหาข้ออ้างในการใช้อาวุธที่โหดร้ายยิ่งขึ้นต่อกัมพูชา

summary: Cambodia officially requested the UN Security Council to take immediate action against what it terms the 'illegal armed aggression' by Thai forces. The letter detailed the use of heavy weapons, tanks, drones, and fighter jets in attacks along the border starting December 7, which have affected civilian areas and cultural heritage sites.
summaryEn: Cambodia officially requested the UN Security Council to take immediate action against what it terms the 'illegal armed aggression' by Thai forces. The letter detailed the use of heavy weapons, tanks, drones, and fighter jets in attacks along the border starting December 7, which have affected civilian areas and cultural heritage sites.

summary: As Thai citizens rapidly evacuate from Poipet City, located near the border, Cambodian residents express fear that the city, which hosts many casinos and online operations, could become Thailand's next target. summary: The Ministry of Interior announced the complete suspension of all entry and exit movements at the Cambodia-Thailand border, effective immediately, due to the escalating border situation where Thailand is allegedly conducting indiscriminate attacks causing civilian casualties and damage. It advised Cambodian and Thai nationals to remain in their respective host countries until a full ceasefire is in place.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Interior announced the complete suspension of all entry and exit movements at the Cambodia-Thailand border, effective immediately, due to the escalating border situation where Thailand is allegedly conducting indiscriminate attacks causing civilian casualties and damage. It advised Cambodian and Thai nationals to remain in their respective host countries until a full ceasefire is in place.

summary: The ongoing border conflict between Cambodia and Thailand has displaced over 400,000 people, prompting international aid bodies to warn of a growing humanitarian catastrophe. The crisis is severely straining resources, disrupting livelihoods, and has far-reaching humanitarian, economic, and diplomatic consequences.
summaryEn: The ongoing border conflict between Cambodia and Thailand has displaced over 400,000 people, prompting international aid bodies to warn of a growing humanitarian catastrophe. The crisis is severely straining resources, disrupting livelihoods, and has far-reaching humanitarian, economic, and diplomatic consequences.

summary: A campaign was launched to sell souvenirs from the 2023 SEA Games to mark its 2nd anniversary and raise at least $10,000 to help displaced families affected by the border conflict. summary: Senate President Samdech Techo Hun Sen suggested an immediate halt to all cross-border travel for both Cambodian and Thai citizens, citing the ongoing Thai military invasion, attacks, and civilian casualties. This is a significant suggestion from Cambodia's most influential political figure regarding border management during the conflict.

summary: The Ministry of Interior announced the immediate and complete suspension of all entry and exit movements at all Cambodia-Thailand border crossings. This decision cites ongoing Thai aggression causing civilian casualties and damage, and is intended to ensure the safety of Cambodian, Thai, and other foreign nationals. Both Cambodian citizens in Thailand and Thai nationals in Cambodia are advised to stay put until a full ceasefire is in effect.

summary: The Ministry of Interior, on behalf of the Royal Government, issued a notice to completely suspend all entry and exit traffic at Cambodia-Thailand border checkpoints. The decision is effective immediately until further notice, and is based on the continued Thai military aggression and attacks on Cambodian civilian areas and infrastructure. The measure is intended to ensure the safety of all citizens (Cambodian, Thai, and foreign) and advises those already in either country to remain in place.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Interior, on behalf of the Royal Government, issued a notice to completely suspend all entry and exit traffic at Cambodia-Thailand border checkpoints. The decision is effective immediately until further notice, and is based on the continued Thai military aggression and attacks on Cambodian civilian areas and infrastructure. The measure is intended to ensure the safety of all citizens (Cambodian, Thai, and foreign) and advises those already in either country to remain in place.

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense released an update on the Cambodia-Thailand border situation for December 13, 2025. summary: This analytical piece, quoting experts, suggests that the renewed, violent border clashes are rooted in deep, long-standing, unresolved structural political issues, rather than just diplomatic breakdown. One analyst highlights Thai domestic political turmoil and the rise of nationalism as a major factor, arguing that increasing the conflict is seen as a politically safer option for the Thai administration than reaching a compromise. Another analyst suggests Thailand is portraying the clashes as a necessary response to Cambodian aggression to divert attention from its own internal instability.

summary: The Ministry of National Defense issued a summary of the situation from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on December 14. It confirmed Thai forces used artillery and F-16s (dropping two bombs in Thmar Sen village, Nimit commune). Thai infantry attempts to advance were resisted by Cambodian military and police forces in Banteay Meanchey province. Artillery fire was also reported in Oddar Meanchey province.
summaryEn: The Ministry of National Defense provided an update from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on December 14, stating that Thai forces continued attacks using F-16s (dropping two bombs in Thmar Sen village) and artillery in multiple provinces (Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey). The report noted that Thai infantry attempts to advance were resisted by Cambodian military and police forces.

summary: Cambodia’s Ministry of Interior announced the suspension of all entry and exit movements at all Cambodia-Thailand border crossings, effective immediately and until further notice. The press release cited acts of aggression by the Thai side through indiscriminate attacks, resulting in Cambodian civilian casualties and damage to residential areas. The Ministry advised Cambodian citizens in Thailand and Thai nationals in Cambodia to remain where they are until a ceasefire is fully implemented.
summaryEn: Cambodia’s Ministry of Interior announced the suspension of all entry and exit movements at all Cambodia-Thailand border crossings, effective immediately and until further notice. The press release cited acts of aggression by the Thai side through indiscriminate attacks, resulting in Cambodian civilian casualties and damage to residential areas. summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior issued a statement rejecting Thai slander and distortion regarding Cambodia's decision to suspend all entry and exit at the border crossings with Thailand. The Ministry asserts the suspension was a temporary measure to ensure the safety of Cambodian civilians and foreigners due to Thailand's 'brutal aggression and continued use of heavy weapons and warplanes against Cambodia's sovereign territory.'
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior issued a statement rejecting Thai slander and distortion regarding Cambodia's decision to suspend all entry and exit at the border crossings with Thailand. The Ministry asserts the suspension was a temporary measure to ensure the safety of Cambodian civilians and foreigners due to Thailand's 'brutal aggression and continued use of heavy weapons and warplanes against Cambodia's sovereign territory.'

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura, announced three conditions for a ceasefire with Cambodia: 1. Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first; 2. The ceasefire must be implemented in practice; 3. Cambodia must genuinely and sincerely cooperate in clearing landmines. The article cites Thai media 'The Nation' from December 15, 2025.
summaryEn: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura, announced three conditions for a ceasefire with Cambodia: 1. Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first; 2. The ceasefire must be implemented in practice; 3. Cambodia must genuinely and sincerely cooperate in clearing landmines. The article cites Thai media 'The Nation' from December 15, 2025.

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim stated that Malaysia is coordinating diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions along the Thailand-Cambodia border. summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Interior rejected Thailand's accusation that Cambodia's decision to suspend border crossings was a violation of international law and human rights principles. The Ministry asserted that Cambodia's decision was made to ensure the safety of civilians, including Thai nationals, from the 'brutal attacks' by the Thai military along the border.

The Ministry asserted that Cambodia's decision was made to ensure the safety of civilians, including Thai nationals, from the 'brutal attacks' by the Thai military along the border.

summary: Cambodia has condemned Thai airstrikes that reportedly targeted civilian areas, including near a displaced civilians camp in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province—more than 70km from the border. The strikes allegedly forced hundreds of already displaced families to flee again, and Cambodia is calling for international intervention.

summary: The Spokeswoman for Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence stated that Cambodian armed forces remain strong and vigilant against Thai aggression, which she claims is intensifying with the use of cluster bombs, artillery, and toxic gas in several provinces. She called on the international community to condemn Thailand's actions and demand an immediate cessation of hostile activities and withdrawal of forces.

summary: The Russian Embassy in Bangkok denied Thai media reports suggesting Russian citizens were involved as mercenaries in the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. The embassy stated these reports were untrue and risked damaging long-standing Russian-Thai relations, reaffirming Russia's support for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

The embassy stated these reports were untrue and risked damaging long-standing Russian-Thai relations, reaffirming Russia's support for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

summary: Cambodia's Defense Ministry reported that a Thai fighter jet bombed an area near a displaced civilians camp in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province. The Information Minister noted this was the first time Thailand had bombed Siem Reap and was the furthest strike (over 70km from the border) during the renewed clashes, forcing hundreds of displaced families to flee the evacuation site.

The Information Minister noted this was the first time Thailand had bombed Siem Reap and was the furthest strike (over 70km from the border) during the renewed clashes, forcing hundreds of displaced families to flee the evacuation site.

summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that a special meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers, scheduled for Tuesday to address the conflict, has been postponed at the request of both Thailand and Cambodia. Anwar appealed for both countries to stop fighting and confirmed that Malaysia would continue to mediate.

summary: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra reported that as of 6:00 PM on December 15, 2025, a total of 126,204 families, equivalent to 421,853 people, have been displaced across seven provinces due to Thailand's armed aggression along the border, seeking safety away from their homes.
summaryEn: Information Minister Neth Pheaktra reported that as of 6:00 PM on December 15, 2025, a total of 126,204 families, equivalent to 421,853 people, have been displaced across seven provinces due to Thailand's armed aggression along the border, seeking safety away from their homes.
summaryKh: រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីក្រសួងព័ត៌មាន ណាត់ ភក្ត្រា បានរាយការណ៍ថា គិតត្រឹមម៉ោង 6:00 ល្ងាច ថ្ងៃទី 15 ខែធ្នូ ឆ្នាំ 2025 គ្រួសារសរុប 126,204 ស្មើនឹង 421,853 នាក់ បានផ្លាស់ទីលំនៅទូទាំង 7 ខេត្ត ដោយសារការឈ្លានពានប្រដាប់អាវុធរបស់ប្រទេសថៃតាមបណ្ដោយព្រំដែន ហើយបានភៀសខ្លួនចេញពីផ្ទះសម្បែងដើម្បីស្វែងរកសុវត្ថិភាព។

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense stated that the Thai military continued to attack Cambodian forces in Military Region 4 (Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey provinces) on the morning of December 15, 2025, using warplanes, heavy artillery, and tanks in Thma Da, Ta Moan Temple, and Chop Kokir areas. The statement asserted that Cambodian troops and border police remain strong. It also noted that schools in 6 border provinces have been closed, affecting 1,039 schools, 9,797 teachers, and 242,881 students.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense stated that the Thai military continued to attack Cambodian forces in Military Region 4 (Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey provinces) on the morning of December 15, 2025, using warplanes, heavy artillery, and tanks in Thma Da, Ta Moan Temple, and Chop Kokir areas. The statement asserted that Cambodian troops and border police remain strong. It also noted that schools in 6 border provinces have been closed, affecting 1,039 schools, 9,797 teachers, and 242,881 students.

summary: The Ministry of Interior released a statement on impacts of Thai aggression from 6:00 PM Dec 15 to 7:00 AM Dec 16, 2025, reporting no new deaths or injuries in that period. The total casualties since December 7 stand at 15 killed and 76 injured, with 422,698 displaced people. The statement also lists the total number of civilian infrastructure destroyed since the aggression began.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Interior released a statement on the impact of Thai military aggression on civilian areas from the evening of December 15 to the morning of December 16, 2025. It reported no new deaths/injuries in that period, but the total casualties since December 7 are 15 killed and 76 injured, with 422,698 displaced people across seven provinces. The statement also detailed the total destruction of civilian infrastructure, including houses, schools, and temples, since the start of the aggression.

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Defense's spokesperson reported that the Thai military fired heavy shelling indiscriminately from a naval vessel into the O Phluk Damrei area in Pursat province, Military Region 5, between the night of December 15 and the morning of December 16, 2025.
summaryEn: Cambodia's Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport reported that as of December 16, 2025, a total of 1,042 schools in 6 border provinces have been closed due to the conflict, affecting 9,865 teachers and 245,001 students. The article also includes a sub-headline mentioning the Cambodian Ministry of Defense's report of the Thai military firing heavy shelling from a naval vessel into the O Phluk Damrei area in Military Region 5.

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation strongly condemned Thailand's armed aggression, including the use of F-16 fighter jets and airstrikes penetrating 80-90 km into Cambodia. The statement cited civilian loss, displacement of over 400,000 people, and damage to UNESCO sites and civilian infrastructure, calling on Thailand to immediately cease all military operations.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation strongly condemned Thailand's armed aggression, including the use of F-16 fighter jets and airstrikes penetrating 80-90 km into Cambodia. The statement cited civilian loss, displacement of over 400,000 people, and damage to UNESCO sites and civilian infrastructure, calling on Thailand to immediately cease all military operations.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior released a statement detailing the impact of what it calls 'Thai aggression' from December 7 to 1:00 PM on December 16, 2025. The statement reports 15 Cambodian civilians killed and 75 injured. It also states that 423,715 people (127,168 families) have been displaced across seven provinces, and lists damage to civilian infrastructure, including 48 civilian houses, one school, and four pagodas.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior released a statement detailing the impact of what it calls 'Thai aggression' from December 7 to 1:00 PM on December 16, 2025. The statement reports 15 Cambodian civilians killed and 75 injured. It also states that 423,715 people (127,168 families) have been displaced across seven provinces, and lists damage to civilian infrastructure, including 48 civilian houses, one school, and four pagodas.

summary: The Czech Republic's Ambassador to Cambodia, Markéta Kolc Hájková, expressed deep sympathy for Cambodian citizens who have lost lives and been displaced due to the ongoing Cambodia-Thailand border conflict. She conveyed that the Czech Republic is closely following the situation and has a strong belief that the issue will be resolved peacefully through negotiation soon. The statement was made during a meeting with National Assembly President Khoun Sudary.

summary: EuroCham Cambodia issued a statement on December 16 noting that goods transport and supply chains remain stable despite border conflict. However, they are monitoring fuel prices closely. The article also repeats MoD claims that as of December 16, 17 Cambodian civilians have died (including 1 infant) and 77 are injured due to Thai military aggression.

The article also repeats MoD claims that as of December 16, 17 Cambodian civilians have died (including 1 infant) and 77 are injured due to Thai military aggression.

summary: Thailand's Foreign Ministry outlined three conditions for peace talks: Cambodia must publicly declare a ceasefire, demonstrate a verifiable commitment to peace, and cooperate in joint demining efforts. Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded by strongly condemning Thailand's actions as disproportionate aggression, including the use of F-16 jets.
summaryEn: Thailand's Foreign Ministry outlined three conditions for peace talks: Cambodia must publicly declare a ceasefire, demonstrate a verifiable commitment to peace, and cooperate in joint demining efforts. Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded by strongly condemning Thailand's actions as disproportionate aggression, including the use of F-16 jets.

summaryTh: กระทรวงการต่างประเทศของไทยได้กำหนดเงื่อนไข 3 ข้อสำหรับการเจรจาสันติภาพ: กัมพูชาต้องประกาศหยุดยิงอย่างเป็นทางการ แสดงความมุ่งมั่นที่ตรวจสอบได้ต่อสันติภาพ และร่วมมือในการกวาดล้างทุ่นระเบิด รัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศของกัมพูชาตอบโต้โดยประณามการกระทำของไทยว่าเป็นการรุกรานที่เกินกว่าเหตุ รวมถึงการใช้เครื่องบิน F-16.

summary: A conflict update for December 17, 2025, at 9:40 AM, reported fierce fighting in Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey province. It stated that the Cambodian army successfully repelled attempts by Thai infantry to push into Cambodian territory and noted that Thai artillery shelled Sla Kram village.

summary: The Cambodian Defense Ministry stated on Wednesday that the civilian death toll has risen to 17, with 77 injured, due to continued Thai airstrikes and artillery. Attacks were noted in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat provinces involving F-16s and drones.

summary: As of late December 2025, the number of displaced Cambodians has reached 422,698 people (126,508 families) across seven provinces including Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Banteay Meanchey. The Ministry of Education reports that 1,039 schools have been closed, affecting over 242,000 students. Humanitarian organizations like World Vision are calling for urgent aid to address food shortages and trauma among children, describing the scale of displacement as 'unprecedented'.

summary: The Ministry of National Defence issued a report stating that Thai forces continued to violate Cambodian sovereignty from December 16 to 17. In Military Region 5 (Banteay Meanchey/Pursat), Thai infantry supported by tanks attempted to advance into Jock Chey and Prey Chan villages, accompanied by drone strikes and reports of 'toxic smoke'.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense provided a detailed update on the 12th day of conflict. summary: The Ministry of Interior announced on December 18 that the ongoing Thai aggression has resulted in 18 Cambodian civilian deaths and 79 injuries. The conflict has forced nearly 480,000 people (approximately 140,000 families) to flee their homes. Five non-border provinces have reportedly begun receiving these internally displaced persons as the shelling of civilian areas continues.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Interior announced on December 18 that the ongoing Thai aggression has resulted in 18 Cambodian civilian deaths and 79 injuries. The conflict has forced nearly 480,000 people (approximately 140,000 families) to flee their homes. Five non-border provinces have reportedly begun receiving these internally displaced persons as the shelling of civilian areas continues.

summary: In an official statement, the Ministry of National Defense urged Thailand to stop 'lying' about the situation and called for an immediate withdrawal of Thai troops from Cambodian territory. The statement demands that Thailand take responsibility for 'war crimes' and violations of international law following 12 days of aggression.

The statement demands that Thailand take responsibility for 'war crimes' and violations of international law following 12 days of aggression.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a detailed timeline for December 18, 2025, marking the 12th day of conflict. It reports Thai F-16 fighter jets bombed Phnom Kmoch and Peak Sbeak areas in the morning, and Poipet Municipality at 11:06 AM. In the afternoon, multiple bombings were reported in Serei Saophoan city. The ministry also accused Thai forces of using 'poisonous smoke' (gas) in the Preah Vihear and 5 January mountain areas.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a detailed timeline for December 18, 2025, marking the 12th day of conflict. It reports Thai F-16 fighter jets bombed Phnom Kmoch and Peak Sbeak areas in the morning, and Poipet Municipality at 11:06 AM. In the afternoon, multiple bombings were reported in Serei Saophoan city. The ministry also accused Thai forces of using 'poisonous smoke' (gas) in the Preah Vihear and 5 January mountain areas.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense provided a detailed update on the 12th day of conflict. It reports that between 8:00 AM and 3:00 PM on Dec 18, Thai forces used F-16 jets to bomb targets in Poipet and Serey Sophorn. The report also alleges the use of 'toxic smoke' in the Preah Vihear area and mentions 18 civilian deaths, including one infant, since the conflict began.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense provided a detailed update on the 12th day of conflict. It reports that between 8:00 AM and 3:00 PM on Dec 18, Thai forces used F-16 jets to bomb targets in Poipet and Serey Sophorn. The report also alleges the use of 'toxic smoke' in the Preah Vihear area and mentions 18 civilian deaths, including one infant, since the conflict began.

summary: Tens of thousands of Cambodians participated in a massive peace march in Phnom Penh on the 12th day of the border conflict with Thailand. Organized by the Union of Youth Federations of Cambodia (UYFC) and led by Hun Many, the rally called for an end to hostilities and respect for a ceasefire. Official reports indicate the conflict has claimed at least 55 lives so far, including 18 Cambodian civilians and 16 Thai civilians, along with numerous military casualties on both sides.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that since the start of Thai military operations on December 7, 18 civilians have been killed and 498,328 people (151,655 families) have been displaced across Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. Significant damage was reported to civilian infrastructure including schools, health centers, and pagodas. The government called for international intervention to compel Thailand to return to the ceasefire agreement.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that since the start of Thai military operations on December 7, 18 civilians have been killed and 498,328 people (151,655 families) have been displaced across Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. Significant damage was reported to civilian infrastructure including schools, health centers, and pagodas. The government called for international intervention to compel Thailand to return to the ceasefire agreement.

summary: A coalition of 39 non-governmental organizations from both Cambodia and Thailand, known as the Thai-Cambodian People's Alliance for Peace, issued a joint statement on December 19 calling for an immediate end to border hostilities. The groups emphasized that the conflict is causing severe hardship for local villagers, farmers, and workers who have long lived in peace. They urged both governments to respect previous peace agreements and restore normalcy for people living along the border.

They urged both governments to respect previous peace agreements and restore normalcy for people living along the border.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released an update on Dec 19, stating that Thai forces are continuing to violate the Oct 26 peace agreement. In Military Zone 5 (Banteay Meanchey/Pursat), reports include Thai drone strikes in Thma Da and artillery fire from a warship in the same area. The ministry claims Thai forces fired shells into civilian homes in Banteay Mean Rith.

summary: Thai Defense Minister Natthaphon Narkphanit admitted on December 19 that Cambodian forces successfully shot down a Thai military DP-20 surveillance drone. He described the loss as 'regrettable but unavoidable' during military operations. He acknowledged Cambodia's air defense capabilities and stated that security has been tightened across all armed forces units following the incident and the discovery of drones near oil rigs in the Gulf of Thailand.

summary: China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi held telephone calls with his Cambodian and Thai counterparts, Prak Sokhonn and Sihasak Phuangketkeow, on Thursday. China is acting as a mediator, urging both sides to reach a ceasefire before the situation undermines ASEAN unity. Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense also issued a statement condemning Thailand for using F-16s and heavy artillery against schools and civilian areas, insisting that Cambodian military moves are purely defensive. ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn warned that the bloc cannot ignore the fighting which has displaced over 500,000 people.

summary: Internal political observers are urging the ruling Hun family to arrest high-level 'criminal masterminds' within Cambodia. This is seen as a move to strip Thailand of its international diplomatic justification for the border conflict, which Thailand claims is partly about addressing cross-border crime and scam hubs. The article highlights that unless the Cambodian government takes action against these figures, Thailand will continue to use the narrative of law enforcement to justify its military presence and 'invasion' of Khmer territory.

summary: Cambodian analysts and legal experts rejected Thailand's claims that its military operations were intended to suppress online scam gangs. Lawyer Sok Sam Oeun stated that bombing ancient temples and bridges with F-16s has nothing to do with fighting criminals and is instead an attempt to destroy Cambodia's military capacity. Experts accused Thailand of using these narratives to distract from violations of international law and to cover up internal issues.

summary: The Thai government, through its Joint Information Center for the Thai-Cambodian Situation, has expressed hope for a ceasefire before December 25. However, Bangkok insists that Cambodia must first accept three unilateral conditions: 1) Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first, 2) The ceasefire must be subject to physical and continuous investigation, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in joint demining operations. Cambodian analysts have called these conditions 'unacceptable,' arguing that Thailand is the aggressor and should be the one to implement such measures. This development comes as ASEAN Foreign Ministers prepare to meet on December 22 to discuss the conflict.

summary: China’s Special Envoy for Asian Affairs, Deng Xijun, visited Phnom Penh to meet with Prime Minister Hun Manet and other high-ranking officials. summary: Deng Xijun, China's Special Envoy for Asian Affairs, visited Phnom Penh on December 19 to meet with PM Hun Manet and other high-ranking officials including Foreign Minister Prak Sokhann and Defense Minister Tea Seyha. Both sides emphasized the urgent need for an immediate ceasefire. Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to existing bilateral frameworks and international law, while thanking President Xi Jinping for China's mediation efforts. The envoy is conducting shuttle diplomacy between Phnom Penh and Bangkok to restore peace after renewed fighting broke out on December 7.

summary: The United States government has issued a formal travel advisory for the Thailand-Cambodia border region due to ongoing active hostilities. American citizens are strongly advised to avoid all travel within 50 kilometers of the border, specifically naming the provinces of Sisaket and Surin in Thailand, and Banteay Meanchey in Cambodia. The advisory highlights risks from cross-border fire and an unpredictable security situation following renewed fighting that began on December 7, 2025. Travelers currently in the area are urged to stay informed and follow local authority instructions.

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Defense spokesperson Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata reported that a Thai F-16 fighter jet dropped two bombs on the civilian O' Jik Bridge on the night of December 19. summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has called on the media to practice 'responsible reporting' during the ongoing border conflict. He urged editors and journalists to ensure their coverage does not undermine military morale, expose security risks, or disrupt frontline operations. The PM emphasized that while press freedom is respected, national security and the safety of troops must come first during this period of active hostilities.

He urged editors and journalists to ensure their coverage does not undermine military morale, expose security risks, or disrupt frontline operations. The PM emphasized that while press freedom is respected, national security and the safety of troops must come first during this period of active hostilities.

summary: Following high-level talks in Malaysia on December 22, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow announced that Thailand and Cambodia have agreed to hold a General Border Committee (GBC) meeting on December 24, 2025. This diplomatic breakthrough comes as the conflict enters its third week, with the death toll of Cambodian civilians standing at 19 and over 518,000 people displaced from their homes.

summary: A Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur ended without a ceasefire agreement. Thailand demanded Cambodia admit to initiating aggression and cooperate on demining, while Cambodia's Foreign Minister demanded an immediate ceasefire by midnight. Both sides agreed to convene the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 24 to discuss ceasefire implementation.
summaryEn: A Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur ended without a ceasefire agreement. Thailand demanded Cambodia admit to initiating aggression and cooperate on demining, while Cambodia's Foreign Minister demanded an immediate ceasefire by midnight. Both sides agreed to convene the General Border Committee (GBC) on December 24 to discuss ceasefire implementation.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defense reported that despite the diplomatic meeting in Kuala Lumpur, Thai forces continued to attack Cambodian territory on the morning of December 22. At approximately 10:50 AM, Thai military forces allegedly fired about 30 rounds of small arms at civilian homes in Kbal Koh, Poipet. Additionally, heavy shelling involving artillery, tanks, and drones was reported in the Preah Vihear and Ta Moan temple areas between 5:00 AM and 12:00 PM.

summary: A Chinese national was injured on Monday morning during intense shelling by Thai forces in the Phnom Prek and Sampov Loun districts of Battambang province. This development highlights the expanding geographic scope of the conflict beyond the traditional flashpoints of Preah Vihear and Banteay Meanchey.

summary: Following the Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Kuala Lumpur, a joint statement urged both Cambodia and Thailand to exercise maximum restraint and cease all hostilities immediately. The ministers welcomed discussions on a ceasefire and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on December 24, 2025, to discuss implementation and verification of the truce.

The ministers welcomed discussions on a ceasefire and announced that the General Border Committee (GBC) will meet on December 24, 2025, to discuss implementation and verification of the truce.

summary: Kandal Provincial Governor Kuoch Chamroeun has appealed to Cambodians with spacious homes to provide temporary shelter for those fleeing the border violence. The governor emphasized that many fled with almost nothing and urgently need food and basic support.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence reported that the Thai military fired two shells into Poipet city, Banteay Meanchey province, at 8:01 AM on December 23. One shell landed in O Russey Sangkat and another in Nimit Sangkat. The ministry characterized the act as a reckless and indiscriminate attack violating international humanitarian law, while stating that Cambodian forces remain on high alert to defend territorial integrity.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence reported that the Thai military fired two shells into Poipet city, Banteay Meanchey province, at 8:01 AM on December 23. One shell landed in O Russey Sangkat and another in Nimit Sangkat. The ministry characterized the act as a reckless and indiscriminate attack violating international humanitarian law, while stating that Cambodian forces remain on high alert to defend territorial integrity.

summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, during an interview at Mar-a-Lago, designated the Cambodia-Thailand conflict as one of the 'eight wars' his administration is intervening in. He explicitly stated that Thailand started the hostilities first. Meanwhile, Cambodia and Thailand have agreed to a defense official meeting on December 24 to discuss a ceasefire verification.

summary: The civilian death toll in Cambodia has reached 21, with 83 injured, as shelling continues in Banteay Meanchey and surrounding provinces. The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications and the Ministry of Information issued a joint statement urging citizens to stop sharing social media content from Thai sources, labeling it as potential misinformation. Defense Minister Tea Seiha confirmed he would attend the GBC meeting on December 24 to seek a peaceful resolution.

summary: The Cambodian Red Cross (CRC) has dispatched 100 tonnes of rice, drinking water, and other supplies to Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. The move follows reports of over 500,000 Cambodians currently seeking shelter in internal displacement camps.

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Authority (CMAA) has officially rejected allegations from the Thai military that Cambodia is laying new landmines along the border. The CMAA stated that these accusations are based on unilateral claims by the Thai side without evidence. Cambodia maintains that any mine incidents are from older, pre-existing mines from past conflicts.

The CMAA stated that these accusations are based on unilateral claims by the Thai side without evidence. Cambodia maintains that any mine incidents are from older, pre-existing mines from past conflicts.

summary: A planned General Border Committee (GBC) meeting to negotiate an end to border clashes is in doubt as both sides disagree on a venue. Cambodia requested to hold the talks in a neutral third country (Kuala Lumpur), citing security concerns, while Thailand insists the bilateral meeting should proceed in Thailand's Chanthaburi province. Over 80 people have reportedly died since fighting resumed in early December.

summary: Military and defense officials from Cambodia and Thailand are scheduled to meet on December 24, 2025, for a General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The meeting is expected to take place in Chanthaburi, Thailand.

The meeting is expected to take place in Chanthaburi, Thailand.

summary: Fighting continued on the morning of December 24 as the General Border Committee (GBC) secretariat prepared to meet. The Defense Ministry reported that Thai T-50 aircraft dropped four bombs in Banan district, leading to the closure of 241 schools. Military spokesperson Maly Socheata claimed Thai forces used toxic gas drones near Preah Vihear. Displaced Cambodian civilians now exceed 600,000.

summary: Authorities in Banan district, Battambang, have ordered the immediate closure of 83 schools, including 3 high schools and 10 secondary schools, after Thai T-50 fighter jets reportedly dropped 4 bombs in civilian areas of Chhoeu Teal commune. summary: Thailand has proposed three conditions for the GBC talks starting at 4:00 PM today in Chanthaburi. The ministerial meeting on Dec 27 depends on the success of these Secretariat-level talks.

summary: Russian Ambassador Anatoly Borovik presented 2 tonnes of rice, cooking oil, noodles, and water to the Cambodian Red Cross (CRC) to support families displaced by the border conflict. Ambassador Borovik expressed condolences for the loss of life and reaffirmed Moscow's humanitarian commitment to Cambodia.

summary: Military delegates from both nations met at the Ban Phak Kat checkpoint in Thailand's Chanthaburi province on Wednesday afternoon. Led by Major General Nhem Boraden (Cambodia) and General Nuttapong Praokaew (Thailand), the secretariat meeting aims to set the agenda for formal ministerial talks on December 27. The discussions are focused on establishing a ceasefire and monitoring mechanisms under the watch of ASEAN Observer Teams (AOT).

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defense reported that Thai fighter jets dropped cluster bombs in Banteay Meanchey and four bombs into civilian areas in Battambang on Wednesday. Thai Army spokesperson Winthai Suvaree countered that any munitions used were directed strictly at military targets and are not meant to harm civilians. He also noted that neither nation is bound by the Convention on Cluster Munitions as they are not signatories.

He also noted that neither nation is bound by the Convention on Cluster Munitions as they are not signatories.

summary: A wild elephant and her newborn calf were found dead in a pond inside the Preah Rokar-Chep Wildlife Sanctuary in Preah Vihear province on December 22. Environmental authorities and park rangers confirmed the deaths were caused by shrapnel from Thai military shelling. Environment Minister Eang Sophalleth condemned the incident, stating that the conflict is destroying Cambodia's natural resources and biodiversity in addition to human lives.

Environmental authorities and park rangers confirmed the deaths were caused by shrapnel from Thai military shelling. Environment Minister Eang Sophalleth condemned the incident, stating that the conflict is destroying Cambodia's natural resources and biodiversity in addition to human lives.

summary: The civilian death toll in Cambodia has increased to 30 following intensified border clashes. The conflict continues to cause significant displacement along the border regions.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that at 8:41 a.m. on December 25, Thai military forces fired 155mm artillery shells into a civilian residential area in Ta Lei village, Kouk Romiet commune, Thmar Pouk district, Banteay Meanchey province. The attack resulted in the death of one innocent Cambodian civilian. The ministry described the actions as 'indiscriminate' and a violation of international humanitarian law.

summary: The second day of the General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat Meeting began at 9:05 a.m. at the Prom-Pak Kard border crossing between Pailin and Chanthaburi. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. This meeting serves as preparation for the 3rd Special GBC Meeting scheduled for December 27, which will involve the Defense Ministers of both nations.

summary: Electricite du Cambodge (EDC) has joined other national institutions in issuing a formal petition condemning what they term as 'vicious and inhumane' acts by the Thai military. The petition supports the Royal Government of Cambodia's stance and calls for an immediate end to the shelling of innocent civilians along the border.

The petition supports the Royal Government of Cambodia's stance and calls for an immediate end to the shelling of innocent civilians along the border.

summary: On December 25, between 7:00 AM and 10:50 AM, the Thai military reportedly fired 33 heavy artillery shells into Taly village, Thmar Puok district, Banteay Meanchey. The strike killed one civilian and injured seven others. The Cambodian government condemned the attack as a 'cruel and inhumane' violation of international humanitarian law targeting civilian infrastructure.

The strike killed one civilian and injured seven others. The Cambodian government condemned the attack as a 'cruel and inhumane' violation of international humanitarian law targeting civilian infrastructure.

summary: The Cambodian Senate issued a formal resolution condemning Thailand for what it calls a 'brutal and illegal invasion' from December 7 to 24. The statement cites the use of heavy artillery and fighter jets against civilians and historical temples, including Preah Vihear. The Senate claims these acts violate the UN Charter, the 1962 ICJ ruling, and recent ceasefire agreements from July and October 2025.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Senate issued a formal resolution condemning Thailand for what it calls a 'brutal and illegal invasion' from December 7 to 24. The statement cites the use of heavy artillery and fighter jets against civilians and historical temples, including Preah Vihear. The Senate claims these acts violate the UN Charter, the 1962 ICJ ruling, and recent ceasefire agreements from July and October 2025.

summary: Chinese Special Envoy Deng Xijun concluded a shuttle-diplomacy mission (Dec 18-23) to Cambodia and Thailand. He expressed condolences for the 30 Cambodian civilians reported killed as of the morning of Dec 25. China urged both sides to achieve an immediate ceasefire, restore trust, and support ASEAN mediation efforts.
summaryEn: Chinese Special Envoy Deng Xijun concluded a shuttle-diplomacy mission (Dec 18-23) to Cambodia and Thailand. He expressed condolences for the 30 Cambodian civilians reported killed as of the morning of Dec 25. China urged both sides to achieve an immediate ceasefire, restore trust, and support ASEAN mediation efforts.

summary: A coalition of 896 Cambodian Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) submitted a petition to the international community condemning ongoing Thai military assaults. The petition highlights the use of cluster bombs and the destruction of cultural heritage, specifically the Ta Krabei Temple and damage to Preah Vihear Temple. The groups urge the UN and the international community to demand an immediate ceasefire and the withdrawal of Thai forces.

The petition highlights the use of cluster bombs and the destruction of cultural heritage, specifically the Ta Krabei Temple and damage to Preah Vihear Temple. The groups urge the UN and the international community to demand an immediate ceasefire and the withdrawal of Thai forces.

summary: The Cambodian National Assembly issued a petition late December 24 condemning Thailand's 'brutal and inhumane invasion.' The statement claims Thailand has used heavy weapons including F-16 and T-50TH jets, warships, and cluster munitions, with strikes reaching 80–90 kilometers deep into Cambodia. It also accused Thailand of using 'toxic gas' and reported that 30 Cambodian civilians have been killed and over 630,000 displaced as of December 24.
summaryEn: The Cambodian National Assembly issued a petition late December 24 condemning Thailand's 'brutal and inhumane invasion.' The statement claims Thailand has used heavy weapons including F-16 and T-50TH jets, warships, and cluster munitions, with strikes reaching 80–90 kilometers deep into Cambodia. It also accused Thailand of using 'toxic gas' and reported that 30 Cambodian civilians have been killed and over 630,000 displaced as of December 24.

summary: Civil society groups from Cambodia and some Thai citizens are calling for an immediate end to hostilities as civilian casualties mount. summary: A ceasefire agreement is expected to be signed on December 27 following three days of intense negotiations at the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting at the Ban Phakkat/Prom border crossing. Despite ongoing reports of heavy shelling and airstrikes killing 31 civilians so far, Thai Prime Minister Anutin expressed optimism that the defense ministers of both nations will sign the document tomorrow. The agreement reportedly involves mine-clearing and the withdrawal of heavy weapons.

summary: On the night of December 25, 2025, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a telephone conversation with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet. summary: Officials from the Ministry of Information and the state news agency AKP delivered aid and school supplies to approximately 300 families displaced from Koh Kong province. These families fled to Srae Ambel district following Thai military aggression that began on December 13. While some families have started returning home, many remain in temporary shelters at local pagodas (such as Wat Sala Mnang) due to the unstable security situation.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a field report detailing Thai military actions on December 26. It reported that at 5:40 AM, Thai forces shelled Ta Krabey Temple, followed by artillery fire at Ta Moan Temple and Preah Vihear Temple. Most significantly, between 6:08 AM and 7:15 AM, Thai F-16 jets reportedly dropped 40 bombs on Chok Chey village, causing significant destruction. The ministry stated that Cambodian forces are fighting back with 'high vigilance.'

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that the Thai military fired approximately 360 shells into Sok Sang and Prey Chan villages in Banteay Meanchey province between 7:00 am and 2:30 pm on December 26. summary: Cambodia has accused Thai forces of carrying out aerial attacks with F-16 fighter jets dropping dozens of bombs near Chouk Chey village on Friday morning. The attacks caused destruction to civilian homes and infrastructure even as both sides hold talks to ease the conflict that has killed at least 96 people since December 8.

The attacks caused destruction to civilian homes and infrastructure even as both sides hold talks to ease the conflict that has killed at least 96 people since December 8.

summary: Following three days of negotiations in Chanthaburi, the GBC secretariat teams have reached a consensus on a draft joint statement and ceasefire terms. The agreement is set to take effect on December 27. Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Thai Defense Minister will attend the meeting today to finalize the statement under the Kuala Lumpur Agreement framework.

Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Thai Defense Minister will attend the meeting today to finalize the statement under the Kuala Lumpur Agreement framework.

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of December 26 evening, Thai military shelling and bombardment has resulted in a total of 31 deaths and 91 injuries among Cambodian civilians since December 7. The latest casualties include one death in Siem Reap and one injury in Banteay Meanchey. The report highlights severe impacts on civilian areas across multiple border provinces.
summaryEn: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of December 26 evening, Thai military shelling and bombardment has resulted in a total of 31 deaths and 91 injuries among Cambodian civilians since December 7. The latest casualties include one death in Siem Reap and one injury in Banteay Meanchey. The report highlights severe impacts on civilian areas across multiple border provinces.

summary: The Club of Cambodian Journalists (CCJ) distributed protective vests and helmets to 57 journalists from 36 media organizations to ensure their safety while reporting from high-risk zones along the Cambodia-Thailand border. summary: Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Tea Seiha announced that Cambodia and Thailand have agreed on an immediate ceasefire effective from 12:00 PM on December 27, 2025. The agreement, reached during the 3rd Special Meeting of the General Border Committee (GBC) in Pailin, requires both sides to maintain current positions for at least 72 hours to ensure full implementation. ASEAN observers were present at the meeting.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Information issued a clarification regarding rumors that the ceasefire signed on December 27 is only valid for 72 hours. The Ministry stated this is a misconception, affirming that the ceasefire is intended for 'long-term peace.' The 72-hour period mentioned in the accord specifically relates to an observation window after which 18 detained Cambodian soldiers will be released by Thailand.
summaryEn: The Cambodian Ministry of Information issued a clarification regarding rumors that the ceasefire signed on December 27 is only valid for 72 hours. The Ministry stated this is a misconception, affirming that the ceasefire is intended for 'long-term peace.' The 72-hour period mentioned in the accord specifically relates to an observation window after which 18 detained Cambodian soldiers will be released by Thailand.

summary: Foreign Ministers of China, Cambodia, and Thailand met in Yunnan on Dec 28-29. They agreed to consolidate the ceasefire, ensure the full implementation of the Dec 27 Joint Statement, and cooperate on humanitarian de-mining. China pledged to provide support for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT).

They agreed to consolidate the ceasefire, ensure the full implementation of the Dec 27 Joint Statement, and cooperate on humanitarian de-mining. China pledged to provide support for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT).

summary: A day after the ceasefire began, Cambodian refugees have started returning to border villages. However, government officials warn that many areas remain dangerous due to unexploded ordnance and landmines. Returning families face severe economic hardship and the task of rebuilding homes destroyed during the 20 days of fighting.

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet issued a message clarifying that the Dec 27 ceasefire is not a surrender or a trade-off of territorial integrity. He emphasized that the decision was made to prioritize the lives of over 500,000 displaced civilians and soldiers' families. He noted that while Cambodia is a small country, it maintains the right to self-defense, but currently prioritizes the return of children to schools and families to their homes. He stated that 32 civilians have died and 93 were injured in the conflict so far.

summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced on December 29 that, pending any last-minute changes, 18 Cambodian soldiers arrested by Thailand in June 2025 are scheduled for release at 12:00 PM on December 30. The release is a direct result of the ceasefire agreement reached on December 27 and is being coordinated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
summaryEn: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced on December 29 that, pending any last-minute changes, 18 Cambodian soldiers arrested by Thailand in June 2025 are scheduled for release at 12:00 PM on December 30. The release is a direct result of the ceasefire agreement reached on December 27 and is being coordinated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced following a trilateral meeting with China and Thailand in Yunnan that 18 Cambodian soldiers held for 151 days are scheduled for release at 12:00 PM on December 30. This marks the end of the required 72-hour period during which the ceasefire must be fully maintained.

This marks the end of the required 72-hour period during which the ceasefire must be fully maintained.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defence reported that as of December 29, the situation in Military Regions 4 and 5 (bordering Thailand) remains calm following the December 27 ceasefire. However, the ministry emphasized that armed forces remain in place and are maintaining high vigilance to defend national sovereignty.

summary: Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence, Lt. Gen. Mali Socheata, denied Thai claims that over 250 drones from Cambodia violated Thai airspace on December 29. She stated that Cambodia is strictly adhering to the GBC joint statement and the ceasefire, and has issued strict bans on any drone flights in border provinces.

She stated that Cambodia is strictly adhering to the GBC joint statement and the ceasefire, and has issued strict bans on any drone flights in border provinces.

summary: Phnom Penh has proposed an urgent special meeting with Thailand to resume the work of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). The goal is to address stalled border survey and demarcation work following the recent ceasefire agreement. This move is seen as an effort to resolve underlying territorial disputes that triggered the recent armed conflict.
summaryEn: Phnom Penh has proposed an urgent special meeting with Thailand to resume the work of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). The goal is to address stalled border survey and demarcation work following the recent ceasefire agreement. This move is seen as an effort to resolve underlying territorial disputes that triggered the recent armed conflict.

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized in a national message that the ceasefire is not a surrender or cession of territory. He stated that the decision was made to protect the lives of civilians, noting that 32 civilians have been killed and 93 injured in the conflict so far. He highlighted that the international boundary remains governed by existing treaties and the ceasefire allows half a million displaced people to return home.

He highlighted that the international boundary remains governed by existing treaties and the ceasefire allows half a million displaced people to return home.

summary: The Ministry of National Defence of Cambodia has categorically rejected Thailand's claim that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai airspace on December 29. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata called the allegations unfounded and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the December 27 ceasefire. She noted that strict instructions have been issued to provincial authorities to prohibit all drone launches.
summaryEn: The Ministry of National Defence of Cambodia has categorically rejected Thailand's claim that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai airspace on December 29. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata called the allegations unfounded and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the December 27 ceasefire. She noted that strict instructions have been issued to provincial authorities to prohibit all drone launches.

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated on December 30 that the 72-hour deadline for full ceasefire implementation has been reached. She reported that the situation along the Cambodia-Thailand border remains calm and stable. This follows the agreement reached during the GBC meeting on December 27.

summary: Following weeks of intense fighting that killed over 100 people and displaced 440,000 Cambodians, Caritas Cambodia has launched an emergency appeal to support 5,000 families in 20 priority camps. The aid includes food, shelter kits, solar lights, and psychosocial support for children traumatized by artillery fire and air strikes. Over 315,000 people are currently sheltering in 200 government evacuation sites facing overcrowding and poor sanitation.

Over 315,000 people are currently sheltering in 200 government evacuation sites facing overcrowding and poor sanitation.

summary: Foreign ministers from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met on December 29 to discuss the border crisis. The priority is to ensure the ceasefire remains effective. They agreed to support the Joint Border Committee (JBC) to demarcate the border according to international law and the UN Charter. China is ready to help with humanitarian demining through the Joint Coordination Task Force (JCTF) and support ASEAN Observers (AOT).
summaryEn: Foreign ministers from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met on December 29 to discuss the border crisis. The priority is to ensure the ceasefire remains effective. They agreed to support the Joint Border Committee (JBC) to demarcate the border according to international law and the UN Charter. China is ready to help with humanitarian demining through the Joint Coordination Task Force (JCTF) and support ASEAN Observers (AOT).
summaryKh: រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសចិន កម្ពុជា និងថៃ បានជួបប្រជុំគ្នាកាលពីថ្ងៃទី 29 ធ្នូ ដើម្បីពិភាក្សាអំពីវិបត្តិព្រំដែន ដោយផ្តល់អាទិភាពដល់ការធានាបទឈប់បាញ់ឱ្យមានប្រសិទ្ធភាព។ ភាគីទាំងបីបានព្រមព្រៀងគាំទ្រដល់គណៈកម្មការចម្រុះខ័ណ្ឌសីមាព្រំដែន (JBC) ដើម្បីបោះបង្គោលព្រំដែនស្របតាមច្បាប់អន្តរជាតិ និងធម្មនុញ្ញ UN។ ចិនត្រៀមខ្លួនជួយលើការបោសសម្អាតមីនមនុស្សធម៌តាមរយៈក្រុមការងារចម្រុះ (JCTF) និងគាំទ្រក្រុមអ្នកសង្កេតការណ៍អាស៊ាន (AOT)។

summary: During a trilateral meeting in Yunnan, China, Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn emphasized that Cambodia and Thailand are permanent neighbors and must ensure peace. He thanked China for its role in facilitating the December 27 ceasefire. China announced 20 million RMB in humanitarian aid for Cambodian IDPs. Sokhonn also held bilateral talks with Thai FM Sihasak Phuangketkeow to reaffirm commitment to the ceasefire and the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement.

He thanked China for its role in facilitating the December 27 ceasefire. China announced 20 million RMB in humanitarian aid for Cambodian IDPs. Sokhonn also held bilateral talks with Thai FM Sihasak Phuangketkeow to reaffirm commitment to the ceasefire and the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement.

summary: As of 5:10 PM on December 30, the 72-hour ceasefire deadline for the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers has passed without their return. Families and provincial governors, including Pailin Governor Ban Sreymom, reported having no information on the release. The situation is complicated by Thai allegations of 250 Cambodian drone incursions and a landmine incident, which Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense has refuted. Over 590,000 Cambodians remain in displacement shelters.

Over 590,000 Cambodians remain in displacement shelters.

summary: Experts and social observers warn that while physical fighting has stopped, a 'Digitalization War' continues online. They claim Thailand is using fake news and AI-generated content to poison the information environment and cause confusion among Cambodians. The Ministry of Information urged citizens to only follow official government sources to avoid falling into psychological traps.

summary: Senate President Hun Sen expressed his deep sympathy for the 18 soldiers who returned after 155 days of separation from their families. He compared their experience to his own struggles and highlighted the government's commitment to 'leaving no soldier behind.' The government has also established a task force to restore infrastructure and livelihoods damaged during the conflict.

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) issued a statement welcoming the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held for 155 days. The soldiers were repatriated via the Prum International Point of Entry in Pailin province on December 31. The ministry stated that this move will contribute to building mutual trust and creating an environment for normalizing relations. The process was observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

summary: King Norodom Sihamoni and the Queen Mother received the 18 recently released Cambodian soldiers at the Royal Palace. The soldiers, who were held by Thai authorities since fighting began in July 2025, were presented with royal gifts. This high-profile reception followed earlier meetings with Prime Minister Hun Manet and Senate President Hun Sen, underscoring the soldiers' status as national heroes in Cambodia.
